lines.text: Do you know how many steps it takes to send one file to the person sitting right next to you?
Sign in. Verify your number. Install the app. Find the contact. Wait for the upload. And then your video arrives, compressed.
Email bounces anything over twenty-five megabytes. Chat apps shrink your photos. And sharing between a phone and a laptop often only works inside one brand.
Then there are the problems you never see. A shared link can stay online for years. A photo can carry the exact place it was taken. And once you hit send, you never really know who opened it.
At work, it gets worse. Files live in one app, tasks in another, and nobody can see what's actually done.
So what do people actually want? No account. No app. Any device. Private by default. Gone when it's done. And proof the right person got it.
That's Orbi Transfer. Open it in any browser, on any device. Drop a file. That's it.
It's locked on your device before it leaves, with AES two fifty six encryption. Your password never leaves your browser. And in thirty minutes or less, it burns.
Up to twenty gigabytes. The original file, never compressed. Whole folders arrive with their structure intact.
Everyone on the same Wi-Fi sees it appear, live. Nearby shows files from your own area. The Open Void is worldwide. Or just scan its QR code.
Need it confidential? Go anonymous. No name, no location, no device. Create a space, get a four letter code, and set a passcode.
Share the code and the passcode. When your receiver joins, you see them appear in the space. Now you know exactly who's inside.
Send the file with its own password and a one time download. The moment they download it, you see it go. One download, then it's gone.
For teams, switch to Work. Make a private space, add tasks, and assign them with an at sign.
Every task has a route of coloured steps. Files are wired straight to their task. One look shows who's doing what, and what's done.
No internet? Offline send works over the same Wi-Fi or a phone hotspot. Scan two codes, and the files go straight across.
Before: six steps, an account, and a compressed copy that lives forever. With Orbi: no account, the original file, gone in thirty minutes.
Orbi Transfer dot com. Drop it, lock it, beam it, burn it.
